Moderna shares plunge after cancer vaccine data leaks — despite positive results
headlines.summary: Moderna released full data on its closely watched cancer vaccine developed with Merck.
headlines.article_text: Moderna stock falls after cancer vaccine data leak Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Moderna shares dropped as much as 25% on Thursday following the leak of partial data on its closely watched cancer vaccine developed with Merck. The stock fell even though the full data, released later Thursday, appeared positive based on Wall Street expectations ahead of the release. The personalized vaccine, known as intismeran autogene, paired with Merck's immunotherapy Keytruda reduced the risk of recurrence or death in certain melanoma patients by 42% compared with Keytruda alone. In this article MRNA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Timon Schneider | SOPA Images | Lightrocket | Getty Images Moderna shares dropped as much as 25% on Thursday following the leak of partial data on its closely watched cancer vaccine developed with Merck . Shares of both drugmakers fell even though the data, released in full later Thursday following the leak, appeared meaningful for patients and positive relative to Wall Street expectations. The personalized vaccine, known as intismeran autogene, paired with Merck's immunotherapy Keytruda reduced the risk of recurrence or death in certain melanoma patients by 42% compared with Keytruda alone. The data also showed that the shot along with Keytruda reduced the risk of cancer spreading to distant parts of the body or death by 38%, compared with just the immunotherapy. The companies said about 82% of patients who received the personalized cancer vaccine alongside Keytruda were alive without their melanoma returning at two years after receiving the shot, compared with 70% of those who received Keytruda alone. "This is a huge development for our patients," said Dr. Hussein Tawbi, a melanoma expert and trial investigator at the University of Texas MD ​Anderson Cancer Center, about the results. He said that the added benefit of the vaccine also comes with much milder toxicity, or side effects like injection-site pain, compared to other cancer treatments. The detailed phase 3 trial results were set to be presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology conference this weekend. "Whenever you put a therapy on top of something that works really well, like Keytruda, sometimes it's harder to show additional benefit. We have no problems of showing additional benefit here," Dr. Dean Li, Merck Research Laboratories president, said in an interview ahead of the results. The benefit appeared even larger after the six-month vaccine regimen, with a separate analysis showing a 58% reduction in risk of recurrence or death. The companies say it is still too early to determine whether the treatment helps patients live longer overall. Several analysts acknowledged investors' elevated expectations ahead of the release, but noted that the data is overall positive. "We assert this relative reduction in recurrence/death is clinically meaningful," BMO Capital Markets analyst Evan Seigerman said in a research note on Thursday following the leak. "Such a [stock] reaction likely reflects inflated expectations into the full data release, rather than a true indictment on the efficacy of the combo therapy." Oncologists and investors see the targeted vaccine as a possible breakthrough treatment, with the potential to be used to treat other forms of cancer in the future. Merck and Moderna are studying the vaccine in several trials across other tumors, such as non-small cell lung cancer, bladder cancer and renal cell carcinoma. But Li acknowledged the companies have more work to show the product can be effective across tumor types. "I can dream of creating a log cabin, but we got some wood chops, and we've just knocked down one tree," Li said. "Knocking one tree does not give you a cabin or a village." For now, the vaccine is not far from potentially entering the market for the first time and reaching melanoma patients. In an interview ahead of the results, Moderna CEO Stéphane Bancel said the company is finishing a filing with regulators to get the drug fully approved next year. "It's a very, very happy moment for the field, for patients," he said. The shot is designed to target the specific mutations in each patient's tumor rather than using a one-size-fits-all approach. The idea is to train the immune system to recognize and kill those unique cancer markers and then pair that response with Keytruda, which helps the body attack the cancer more effectively. It could also offer Moderna a critical additional commercial product in its pipeline, following vaccines for Covid-19, the flu and respiratory syncytial virus. In a research note Thursday, UBS analysts said "this is overall a strong data set" and gives more confidence in upcoming studies of the vaccine in kidney and bladder cancers. They added the stock reaction may be due more to massive expectations than disappointing data. Against the backdrop of those high expectations, Moderna shares have spiked more than 530% year-to-date as of Thursday afternoon. Shares of Merck, a much larger drugmaker, fell by about 1% on Thursday. The company's stock has climbed nearly 41% this year. Since the vaccine is personalized, the complicated manufacturing process can take six weeks. But Merck CEO Robert Davis told CNBC last week that the company believes it can shorten that timeline in the future, potentially allowing the shot to reach more patients more quickly. Stephanie Keith | Bloomberg | Getty Images American Express is cutting thousands of employees as the leading credit card company prepares for artificial intelligence to take over more of its internal processes. Amex is eliminating 5% of its global workforce and taking a $336 million restructuring charge, CEO Stephen Squeri told analysts Friday on the company's third-quarter earnings call. The firm had almost 77,000 employees at the end of 2025. CFO Christophe Le Caillec told CNBC in an interview that the restructuring charge was to make American Express "leaner, more agile, and also to prepare for AI." "You don't want to automate processes that are not optimally structured," Le Caillec said. "So what we're doing here is to reduce layers and increase spans of controls, so that we can automate and take advantage of AI in the coming quarters and the coming years." The Amex announcement reflects a broader trend across financial services, where banks are working to replace repetitive roles with AI automation. On Thursday, Barclays confirmed plans to trim 5,000 jobs — also roughly 5% of its staff — in another tech-driven cost initiative. The moves come even as the sector is enjoying robust profits from growing consumer spending and resilient credit. During the analyst call, Squeri said that the charge was to improve the company's efficiency. "We've got good momentum, but to accelerate innovation and win over the next few years, we needed to become [a] more agile and efficient organization," Squeri said. "We believe this exercise will help us operate and execute more effectively and give us greater capacity to invest in our business priorities," he said. This story is developing. headlines.summary: Shares of companies with multiple restaurant brands like Brinker and Darden are outperforming single-chain stocks like McDonald's and Chipotle.
headlines.article_text: Darden, Brinker stocks rise ahead of restaurant earnings Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Shares of companies with multiple restaurant brands like Brinker and Darden are outperforming single-chain stocks like McDonald's and Chipotle. Major restaurant companies will start to report their quarterly earnings next week and offer a glimpse at how those trends are playing out. Some Wall Street analysts say owning multiple brands can insulate a company from weakness at one chain, but focusing on one business can also help it perform better. In this article DRI EAT QSR Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A sign is posted in front of a Chili's restaurant in Rohnert Park, California, on Dec. 13, 2024. Justin Sullivan | Getty Images Restaurant stocks have split sharply this year. And it could be tied to how many brands they own. Shares of Brinker International , Darden Restaurants and Restaurant Brands International are up roughly 32%, 18% and 12%, respectively, year to date. Those companies all own more than one restaurant chain, with brands collectively ranging from Chili's to Olive Garden, LongHorn Steakhouse, Burger King and Tim Hortons. Meanwhile, stocks like McDonald's , Chipotle , Cava , Wendy's , Shake Shack and Domino's have all dropped this year, with several down double-digit percentages. Those companies all have one core chain to their names. Those share moves underscore what some analysts see as the benefits of a diversified restaurant business, especially at a time when any misstep can make cash-strapped consumers go elsewhere when they dine out. Investors will get another look at how operating multiple chains — or not — is affecting performance when major restaurant companies report quarterly results starting next week. One company that could be watching is Inspire Brands, the owner of chains like Dunkin', Buffalo Wild Wings and Jimmy John's, which is moving toward going public . A business built around one main restaurant concept depends more heavily on that brand holding consumers' attention, whereas a company with a portfolio has other potential sources of sales if one brand loses momentum. That cushion can be critical, but only if another chain is strong enough to pick up the slack, according to some Wall Street analysts. "Darden is probably the best case of the scale and size and diversity of business," said Nick Setyan, a restaurant analyst at Mizuho Securities. "If one business isn't doing well, the other ones are." Igor Golovniov | Lightrocket | Getty Images Setyan said that dynamic has played out between Darden's key brands — Olive Garden and LongHorn Steakhouse — over recent quarters. LongHorn's growth has outpaced Olive Garden's for months, and in the latest reported quarter, LongHorn's comparable sales rose 6.2% compared with Olive Garden's 1.1%. KeyBanc Capital Markets also cited the range of Darden's portfolio as a positive in an October research note, saying it gives the company "exposure to a broad range of consumers." The company's fine dining and casual offerings can be beneficial in a K-shaped economy where consumer spending can vary by income. The firm has a buy-equivalent rating on Darden and a $237 price target, compared with a price of around $215 as of Thursday. Restaurant Brands International, similarly, offers exposure to different categories and markets through Burger King, Tim Hortons and Popeyes. But its portfolio does not fully insulate the company from a weak brand. Tim Hortons owner to purchase Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen. The parent company of Tim Hortons and Burger King said it will pay US$1.8 billion cash to buy the Popeyes chain. Randy Risling | Toronto Star | Getty Images In the second quarter, Burger King's U.S. comparable sales accelerated to 8.5%, from 5.8% in the first quarter, while Tim Hortons' Canadian comparable sales slowed to just 0.1%, from 1.5% over the same period. That left Burger King's turnaround carrying more of the portfolio as Tim Hortons stalled. Setyan said Burger King's recent strong performance has been central to the company's momentum, helped by its ability to better communicate its value items to customers as McDonald's sales growth slowed. "If it weren't for Burger King's current performance, I don't know if [Restaurant Brands] would be going so well," he said. Mizuho initiated coverage of Restaurant Brands on Oct. 20 with a buy-equivalent rating and an $85 price target. Shares traded at about $76 as of Thursday. A focus on one brand can also be a strength. Starbucks and Cheesecake Factory have been restaurant-stock standouts this year, showing how a clear brand identity and investment can drive outperformance when execution and customer demand click. Their shares have climbed 21% and nearly 123%, respectively, this year. And Starbucks, for its part, said it would not buy Chipotle after reportedly considering a massive buyout that would have diversified its business. Both stocks faltered even though the full data which was released Thursday appeared meaningful for patients and positive relative to Wall Street expectations. Deckers – Shares of the shoemaker are down 6.7% after it reported fiscal second quarter earnings late Thursday that missed analyst expectations. Revenue for the quarter ended Sept. 30 was $1.43 billion compared to the $1.51 Wall Street was expecting. Revenue from top brands including HOKA and UGG missing FactSet expectations. Telecom stocks – Shares of AT & T dropped 4.2%, T-Mobile fell 4.3% while Verizon decreased 3.6% on a Bloomberg News report that SpaceX is in private talks to lease 80,000 cell towers. SpaceX is attempting to build the fourth nationwide wireless carrier by combining its Starlink direct-to-device network with ground infrastructure, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with discussions. Cell tower owners Crown Castle jumped 7.6% and American Tower popped 5.5%. Crown Castle is one of the companies involved in the talks, Bloomberg said. SpaceX — Shares of the Elon Musk space and AI company were also getting a boost from an upgrade on Wall Street. PhillipCapital double upgraded the shares to buy from sell, raising its price target all the way to $250 from $75, citing surprising gains for its AI business. The new price target represents a 70% gain from here. Bloom Energy – shares are down 2.5% after the energy technology solutions provider for data centers reported third quarter earnings late Thursday. Despite beating on the top and bottom line and raising its full-year 2026 earnings per share guidance, what stirred fear among investors was the reported negative free cash flow for the quarter. Comfort Systems – shares are down 3.6% despite delivering a top and bottom line beat for its third quarters earnings late Thursday. Margins for the heating, ventilation, and air conditioning provider came in below expectations. As an offset, the company's third quarter backlog increased 90% year over year. Western Digital – Shares are moving 3.4% lower in the premarket Friday despite reporting strong earnings late Thursday. The data storage device provider a beat on the top lines while delivering a dividend increase. Management said fiscal 2027 is off to a good start, but there are broader investor concerns around the level of demand and AI-driven spending.
